I realize there are vertical walls for the pockets and some corner fillets involved. Other planes seem to correspond to handle dimensions and transitions.
**Analyzing structural components**

I'm identifying planes and features in this structure. Planes 20 and 22, located at x=-10 and x=10 for z=-110 to -150, seem to be side faces of an open-end gap. The open end head is likely between z=-150 and z=-101. Faces 16 and 23 are large cylinders which align with the outer circular perimeter of the open-end head, giving it a C-shape. Smaller cylinders appear to be transitions between the shank and head, with specific dimensions noted for the ring end and through-hole features.
**Mapping cylinder and plane features**

I’m analyzing cylinders 11 and 13 with a radius of 5 around z=-0.3, which represent fillets between the shank and the ring end. The coordinate system is organized such that the ring is at the positive end (z=0 to 25.9) and the open end is at the negative end (z=-150 to -101). The handle is situated between z=-100 and 0. Planes 20 and 22 seem to form vertical sides of the jaw opening, likely creating a vertical slot with a width of 20.
**Clarifying jaw and slot structure**

I'm looking at the inner jaw faces that grip the nut, and Plane 18 at z=-110 appears to mark the bottom of the slot, possibly with a rounded end. It spans from x=-5 to x=5, giving a flat inside end. I think the open slot might have a semicircular bottom, yet the plane at z=-110 is flat and perpendicular to z, suggesting it terminates there. The outer perimeter of the open-end head is formed by cylinders 16 and 23, which are large with radii of 25.8 and 25.97.
**Defining sections and faces**

I’m identifying the different components of the design. The shank side faces are represented by planes 10 and 14, which create the straight sides of the handle. I notice that the outer transition from the shank to the open head involves certain cylinders, and there might not be any planes at specific z-values. 

I’ll categorize the parts into logical sections: Section A can include the broad top and bottom faces, while Section B will focus on the open-end head. Other sections will cover the handle, ring end, and handle pocket recess. I’m mapping the adjacency of faces for pockets and open-end heads, ensuring a clear order for how they connect. This approach helps in organizing the entire structure neatly.
**Addressing adjacency and sections**

I'm working on the adjacency details between certain cylinders, particularly around the opening edges. They may not touch directly, but are likely separated by jaw tips, connecting through top and bottom faces. In organizing the sections, I plan to define subgroups for the exterior and internal slots. 

I’m also listing features like the handle shank, ring end, and the top pocket recess. Each will need its own set of relationships based on their functions, such as how the handle transmits loads between components. I’ll ensure a logical face coding system and correct ordering for visibility. Plus, I need unique RGB colors for clarity!
**Organizing relationships and features**

I'm planning to include key features in each section and a summary in the part description. It makes sense to add a list under "part.description" while also detailing features within each section. There are no minor faces to consider.

Next, I'll craft the relationships for each section, specifying connections like how the handle shank transmits loads to both the open-end head and the ring end. part.name: Combination-style wrench body (open-end + ring-end) with top pocket
part.description: Single solid, constant thickness plate-like wrench. Major functional features: (1) open-end jaw interface at one end, (2) ring/box-end circular interface at the other end with a through hole, (3) straight handle/shank connecting the ends, (4) rectangular recessed pocket on the top face for weight reduction/branding/grip, with filleted internal corners. Structural features: large top/bottom planar faces (constant thickness), outer perimeter made of planar side faces plus large cylindrical arc side faces at the ends, multiple cylindrical blend/fillet side faces.
part.symmetry_note: Approximate mirror symmetry about the longitudinal center plane (x=0) for the external outline; not symmetric through thickness (y mid-plane) due to the one-sided top pocket recess.

Section.name: Global top & bottom broad faces
features included: Boundary edges that define the overall outline opening and pocket opening
Section.function intent: Provide the main bearing/finish surfaces and define overall thickness; act as the primary faces from which recesses and side walls are bounded.
Section.physical behavior: Carries in-plane bending and torsion through the wrench length; distributes stress across the part thickness and provides flat reference for machining/printing and handling.
Section.geometry: Two large, nearly full-outline planar faces at y=15 (top) and y=0 (bottom), spanning the entire wrench silhouette including both ends and handle.
Section.location: Entire part: outermost faces normal to the thickness direction (±Y).

major_faces.name: Top face (overall)
major_faces.description: Global top planar face at y=15 forming the upper boundary of the wrench body and the opening boundary of the pocket.

major_faces.name: Bottom face (overall)
major_faces.description: Global bottom planar face at y=0 forming the lower boundary of the wrench body.

Section.name: Open-end jaw head
features included: Inner corner blends/fillets of the jaw slot
Outer perimeter arc surfaces of the head
Section.function intent: Engage and constrain a hex fastener across flats using the open jaw; provide leverage via the handle while maintaining strength at the head.
Section.physical behavior: Resists spreading at the jaws under torque by placing the head in bending and localized bearing at the jaw faces; outer head arc and blend fillets reduce stress concentration and transmit load into the handle.
Section.geometry: C-shaped/open head formed by large outer cylindrical side surfaces (outer perimeter arcs), plus an internal slot defined by two planar jaw faces (x=±10), a planar end face (z=-110), and cylindrical corner blends (r=5). Transition from handle to head uses additional cylindrical blend surfaces (r=5).
Section.location: One end of the wrench (most negative Z region, around z≈-150 to -100).

major_faces.name: Left jaw gripping face
major_faces.description: Planar inner jaw face at x=-10 that contacts one flat of the fastener.

major_faces.name: Left inner jaw corner fillet
major_faces.description: Cylindrical blend (r=5) between left jaw face and the slot end region.

major_faces.name: Jaw slot end face
major_faces.description: Planar end/stop face at z=-110 closing the inner end of the jaw slot.

major_faces.name: Right inner jaw corner fillet
major_faces.description: Cylindrical blend (r=5) between slot end face and right jaw face.

major_faces.name: Right jaw gripping face
major_faces.description: Planar inner jaw face at x=10 that contacts the opposite flat of the fastener.

major_faces.name: Left head-to-handle blend
major_faces.description: Cylindrical blend (r=5) smoothing the transition from handle side to left side of the head region.

major_faces.name: Left outer head perimeter arc
major_faces.description: Large cylindrical side surface defining the left portion of the outer head circumference (outer profile).

major_faces.name: Right outer head perimeter arc
major_faces.description: Large cylindrical side surface defining the right portion of the outer head circumference (outer profile).

major_faces.name: Right head-to-handle blend
major_faces.description: Cylindrical blend (r=5) smoothing the transition from handle side to right side of the head region.

Section.name: Handle / shank outer sides
features included: Straight handle side faces (constant width region)
Primary load path between the two ends
Section.function intent: Provide leverage arm and transmit user-applied torque between the two wrench ends.
Section.physical behavior: Acts as a beam in bending and torsion; side faces bound the section modulus and stiffness and carry shear flow under torque.
Section.geometry: Two long planar side faces (x constant) spanning most of the handle length between head transition and ring transition.
Section.location: Central region between open-end head and ring-end (approximately mid Z).

major_faces.name: Left handle side face
major_faces.description: Long planar side face at x=-10.0935 defining the left edge of the shank.

major_faces.name: Right handle side face
major_faces.description: Long planar side face at x=10 defining the right edge of the shank.

Section.name: Ring / box-end head (with through hole) and transition
Section.function intent: Provide a closed ring interface to engage a fastener with improved contact and reduced slip; provide clearance through the bore for the fastener head/nut profile.
Section.physical behavior: Loads from the fastener are carried as bearing stresses around the bore and distributed into the ring and into the handle through blended transitions; the closed ring increases stiffness compared with an open jaw.
Section.geometry: Outer cylindrical side surface (ring perimeter), inner cylindrical side surface (through hole), and two cylindrical blend/transition surfaces (r=5) from handle to ring region.
Section.location: Opposite end from open jaw (positive Z region, around z≈0 to 26).

major_faces.name: Left ring transition fillet
major_faces.description: Cylindrical blend (r=5) on the left side transitioning handle width into the ring-end region.

major_faces.name: Ring outer perimeter
major_faces.description: Outer cylindrical side surface defining the ring-end outer diameter (radius ~14.92).

major_faces.name: Right ring transition fillet
major_faces.description: Cylindrical blend (r=5) on the right side transitioning handle width into the ring-end region.

major_faces.name: Ring through-hole wall
major_faces.description: Inner cylindrical surface of the ring-end bore (radius 10) providing clearance for fastener insertion.

Section.name: Top pocket recess (handle cavity)
features included: Rectangular recessed pocket on top face
Section.function intent: Reduce mass and/or provide a recessed area for label/branding and improved grip/handling without changing outer envelope.
Section.physical behavior: Creates a local thickness reduction on one side; shifts neutral axis slightly and can concentrate stress at pocket ends—mitigated by corner fillets and smooth wall/floor transitions.
Section.geometry: Shallow rectangular recess open to the top face: a planar floor at y=14, four planar walls, and four small cylindrical fillet bands (r=1) at the inside corners.
Section.location: On the top face of the handle/shank, centered laterally, spanning a long portion of the handle length (approximately z≈-97 to -6).
